value_proposition: Helps users discover and explore the vast world of isomeric words by rearranging the letters of their favorite English words, providing an engaging and challenging experience.
consumption_model: Interactive Web UI with a single-click launch, pre-seeded demo data, and clear onboarding within 60 seconds, with optional progression to the next word based on completion of all possible anagrams.
packaging_format: Turnkey WEB_UI package: root '/' serves interactive UI, CLI launcher included, pre-seeded realistic sample data, and /api/export JSON endpoint for easy data sharing, with consideration for edge cases such as repeated letters and special characters.
onboarding_experience: Zero-config startup: The app launches immediately with pre-seeded demo data, and the user is presented with a clear and concise onboarding message.
Immediate visual feedback: The app displays a loading animation while the demo data is being loaded, and the user is notified when the data is ready.
Clear instructions: The app provides clear instructions on how to use the anagram feature, including examples and tutorials.
Optional tutorial: The app offers an optional tutorial that guides the user through the anagram feature, with interactive examples and feedback.
Progression guidance: The app provides guidance on how to progress to the next word, including options to complete all possible anagrams or move on to the next word.
distribution_channels: Local execution: The app can be run directly from the local file system using a single command.
Portable .zip handoff: The app can be packaged in a portable .zip file for easy distribution and deployment.
Docker containerization: The app can be containerized using Docker for easy deployment and scaling.
Cloud deployment: The app can be deployed to cloud platforms, such as AWS or Google Cloud, for easy access and scalability.
gtm_readiness_checklist: Developers must ensure that all dependencies are properly installed and configured for the WEB_UI package, including consideration for edge cases such as repeated letters and special characters.
UI Designers must create a visually appealing and intuitive interface for the app, with clear and concise instructions for the user, including examples and tutorials.

QA Engineers must thoroughly test the app for functionality, usability, and performance, ensuring that it meets the required standards, including edge cases such as repeated letters and special characters.
DevOps Engineers must ensure that the app is properly packaged and deployed to the desired distribution channels, including cloud deployment options.

Tech Writers must create clear and concise documentation for the app, including user guides, FAQs, and release notes, with consideration for edge cases such as repeated letters and special characters.
